rounds.text: Om Galaxy Ltd is trading at a modest P/E of 16 [E1] while delivering exceptional profitability that vastly outpaces sector benchmarks, evidenced by an ROE of 22.84% against a sector average of 6.63% [E8] and an ROCE of 23.81% versus 6.4% [E9]. The business is generating substantial operating cash flow of Rs 35 Cr in Mar 2026 [E23], with robust cash conversion of 2.06x demonstrating that reported profits are fully backed by cash [E22]. Furthermore, the company exhibits improving operational efficiency as debtor days have dropped from 123 to 88.2 days [E39] and working capital requirements have significantly reduced from 52.5 days to 22.7 days [E40]. A reverse DCF indicates that the current market price only prices in a modest 6.4% earnings growth, which sits well below the historical 3-year compounded profit growth of 17% [E15, E35]. Conceded: [E24].

Despite solid headline profitability metrics, Om Galaxy Ltd carries significant underlying financial risks that warrant caution. Most notably, the company generated a negative free cash flow of Rs -12 Cr in Mar 2026 [E24], highlighting a stark disconnect between reported accounting profits and actual cash generation after capital outlays. This cash burn is exacerbated by rising debt, with total borrowings increasing to Rs 38 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 25 Cr a year earlier [E27]. Furthermore, capital expenditure is surging aggressively, evidenced by a 1500.0% spike in Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) to Rs 16 Cr [E28], which threatens to pressure liquidity further if these projects face execution delays or fail to yield adequate returns. Operational stability also remains a concern, as the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are both classified as inconsistent [E20, E21], and the current ratio sits at a relatively thin buffer of 1.20x [E26]. Finally, shareholders receive no immediate cash return on their investment, as the dividend yield stands strictly at 0.00% [E3]. conceded: [E33]

The bear points to a negative free cash flow of Rs -12 Cr [E24], but this cash burn is entirely deliberate and productive, driven by a massive 1500.0% surge in CWIP to Rs 16 Cr [E28] representing active growth spend rather than operational distress. While borrowings increased to Rs 38 Cr [E27], leverage remains at a modest 0.47x [E25], and the profits are heavily backed by a robust operating cash flow of Rs 35 Cr [E23] and a strong 2.06x cash conversion rate [E22]. The thin current ratio of 1.20x [E26] provides an adequate buffer, especially as working capital requirements have dramatically improved from 52.5 days down to 22.7 days [E40]. Although operating margins are labeled inconsistent [E20, E21], the actual operating margin has expanded by 5 percentage points to reach 26% [E19], showcasing fundamental margin enhancement over time. conceded: [E3]

The bull dismisses the negative free cash flow of Rs -12 Cr as productive spending, but ignores the concrete burden of rising debt, which climbed from Rs 25 Cr to Rs 38 Cr in a single year [E27]. While the bull points to a 1500% surge in Capital Work in Progress to Rs 16 Cr as evidence of deliberate growth [E28], this massive capex build-up has directly drained cash and expanded liabilities without yet proving its return. The bull highlights a modest leverage ratio of 0.47x [E25], but overlooks the reality that borrowings grew alongside a current ratio that sits at a thin 1.20x buffer [E26]. Furthermore, while the bull defends the margin expansion [E19], the evidence explicitly states that the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are inconsistent [E20, E21]. Finally, the bull concedes the lack of shareholder returns through a 0.00% dividend yield [E3], leaving investors entirely dependent on future execution that is currently clouded by cash burn.
